blocks.text: Imagine a farmer in Nigeria watching his crops wash away after heavy rains. This is a reality for many due to soil erosion. Understanding soil conservation is crucial for sustainable agriculture.

blocks.markdown: Soil conservation refers to the practices that protect soil from erosion and depletion. In Nigeria, where agriculture is a primary source of livelihood, implementing effective soil conservation techniques can significantly enhance productivity.

blocks.title: What is Soil Erosion?
blocks.text: Soil erosion is the process by which the top layer of soil is removed due to factors like water, wind, and human activities. It can lead to reduced soil fertility and agricultural productivity.

blocks.markdown: There are two main types of soil erosion: **water erosion** and **wind erosion**. Water erosion occurs when rainwater or surface runoff washes away soil, while wind erosion happens when strong winds blow away loose soil particles. Both types can severely impact agricultural land.

blocks.title: Calculating Soil Loss Due to Erosion
blocks.prompt: A farmer notices that his field loses about 5 tons of soil per hectare each year due to water erosion. How much soil will be lost from a 10-hectare field in one year?

steps.text: Identify the soil loss per hectare: 5 tons.
Multiply by the total area: 5 tons/hectare × 10 hectares = 50 tons.

blocks.answer: The farmer will lose 50 tons of soil from his 10-hectare field in one year.

blocks.markdown: To combat soil erosion, several conservation practices can be employed. These include **contour ridging**, **cover cropping**, **terracing**, and **afforestation**. Each method has its advantages and can be tailored to specific agricultural conditions.

blocks.title: Key Practices for Soil Conservation
blocks.text: Remember that contour ridging involves plowing along the contours of the land to reduce runoff, while cover cropping uses specific plants to protect the soil. Understanding these methods can help in exam scenarios.

points: Soil erosion is a significant threat to agricultural productivity in Nigeria.
Implementing soil conservation practices is essential for maintaining soil health and ensuring sustainable farming.
